title: Matrix inversion: ManimGL animation, Remotion lesson and revision pack
rawUserTask: Use Three Blue One Brown's tool to create a video on matrix inversion using Remotion, plus cheat sheets and flash cards.
task: Produce a clear original 60–120 second lesson on matrix inversion for a first linear algebra student. Interpret '3Blue1Brown's tool' as 3b1b's ManimGL and say that assumption in the README. Generate the lesson storyboard, a printable cheat sheet and usable flashcards through the Hands specialist. Render actual ManimGL geometry clips and composite the finished video with Remotion through the trusted media renderer. Cover a linear transformation as movement of basis vectors, the inverse undoing that transformation, the identity condition, the nonzero-determinant condition, a worked 2x2 numerical example, solving Ax=b, and why a singular matrix cannot be inverted. Use original wording and animations, cite the provided primary sources, and never imply endorsement by 3Blue1Brown. Return to Jev for bounded render/validate/delivery actions. Inspect the actual MP4 and rendered revision pages before claiming success.
assumptions: The requested 3Blue1Brown tool is ManimGL (3b1b/manim), not the separate Manim Community distribution.
This is an introductory explanation of real square matrices, with 2x2 worked examples. General non-square pseudoinverses are outside scope.
A silent video with burned-in captions and a transcript is acceptable, or local clearly synthetic narration may accompany it. Do not imitate Grant Sanderson's voice.
contentRequirements: Explain that A maps basis vectors to its columns, using column-vector convention consistently.
Show at least one actual ManimGL animation of a nonsingular numeric A followed by computed A inverse, with the grid and basis vectors returning to their starting positions.
State A inverse A = A A inverse = I for a square invertible matrix; order of composition matters.
State for a 2x2 A=[[a,b],[c,d]], det(A)=ad-bc and A inverse=(1/det(A))*[[d,-b],[-c,a]] when determinant is nonzero.
Use one internally consistent numerical example across the video, cheat sheet and at least two flashcards. Independently check both products give I and Ax=b for the displayed solution.

Show or explain a singular example with dependent columns and determinant zero; lost information means no unique reverse transformation. A singular Ax=b may have no solutions or infinitely many, so do not say it always has no solution.
Explain algebraic use x=A inverse b, while noting that numerical software usually solves the linear system directly rather than explicitly forming the inverse.
Give the cheat sheet a short self-test with answers and the flashcards retrieval-practice questions rather than merely copied paragraphs.
artifacts: storyboard.json matching workflows/media/storyboard.ts, created by the allowed Hands specialist rather than a fixed completed fixture
actual ManimGL asset MP4(s), renderer manifest, source URLs and original lesson transcript
cheat-sheet.html: self-contained printable document with definitions, formulas, worked example, singular warning and short self-test answers
flashcards.html: self-contained keyboard-usable reveal/hide answers, at least 10 original question/answer cards
flashcards.csv or flashcards.json: portable card data with the same questions and answers
README.md explaining local opening, sources, assumptions, tool versions, actual checks and remaining limitations

renderer.matrixInterface: scene.matrix is a numeric 2x2 array with each entry in [-5,5]; scene.visual='matrix'. The trusted renderer computes the determinant and inverse, generates actual ManimGL animation, and composites it in Remotion. No model-generated executable code is passed to Manim.
renderer.output: render-manifest.json has engine versions, timing, artifact hashes, full-decode status, matrix/inverse data and sources; contact-sheet.png plus per-scene stills are for human visual inspection.
renderer.failurePolicy: Missing Manim/OpenGL or failed render is an incomplete task. Do not silently replace Manim with a lookalike SVG animation and call it passed.

handoffRequirements.toAgent: Jev selects a multimedia/math specialist using one allowed model; that agent reasons about the math and writes the lesson/revision artifacts plus bounded JSON storyboard.
handoffRequirements.backToJev: Resume Jev after specialist output to select grounded finite actions: validate manifest/math, render, inspect known artifacts, and deliver/open exact outputs. Record decisions and actual tool outcomes, not only plan text.

rubric.check: The actual Hands run delegates creative work to an allowed model and resumes Jev to execute bounded completion steps; external handcrafted final artifacts do not count.
A complete 60–120 second MP4 is rendered, metadata matches and the entire file decodes; representative frames and motion are inspected.
The artifact uses actual 3b1b ManimGL output and actual Remotion composition, with recorded versions and output asset hashes.
All formulas and worked values are correct; invertibility and singular-system qualifications are accurate; no elementwise-reciprocal misconception or multiplication-order mistake.
Video presents a connected explanation from geometry to algebra to an example. Captions are readable and allow sufficient time; no cropped formula or overloaded slide.
Printable cheat sheet and at least ten usable flashcards exist, load locally and agree with the video. Flashcard reveal/hide interaction works using a keyboard.
Primary sources are cited and original wording/animations are used. Manim interpretation is disclosed; no 3Blue1Brown endorsement/voice-copying claim.
Success report distinguishes mathematical checks, full decode and actual visual inspection; any dependency or playback failure leaves the case incomplete.

performance.guidance: Generate all artifacts in one specialist phase where possible. Use numeric storyboard contracts for safe reusable rendering. Render once after schema/math validation; re-render only for an observed defect.
